questions.q: What real operational problem does a plain folder of Parquet files on S3 fail to solve on its own?
options: Athena cannot read Parquet at all without Iceberg
Parquet files cannot be compressed
S3 cannot store files larger than 5 MB
There's no safe way for a reader to query the data while a writer is mid-update without risking an inconsistent, half-written result
questions.explain: Without a table format tracking a consistent state, a reader querying mid-write can see a partial, inconsistent combination of old and new files.

questions.q: What does an Iceberg snapshot actually represent?
options: A manually triggered export of the table to a different bucket
An immutable, complete, consistent list of exactly which data files make up the table at one point in time
A compressed backup copy of the entire table stored separately
A cached query result for faster repeated reads
questions.explain: A snapshot is metadata — a pointer to the exact set of files representing the table's state — not a data copy.

questions.q: What is Amazon S3 Tables, specifically?
options: A Lambda function that converts CSV files to tables on demand
A separate database engine unrelated to S3 storage
A distinct S3 bucket type (a table bucket) purpose-built for storing tables in Apache Iceberg format, with automatic maintenance
A new file format that replaces Parquet
questions.explain: S3 Tables is a bucket type (table bucket), not a new file format or separate database — it stores Iceberg-format tables with built-in maintenance.

questions.q: What is the real, concrete difference between managing Iceberg tables on a general-purpose S3 bucket versus using S3 Tables?
options: S3 Tables tables cannot be queried by Athena
S3 Tables uses a completely different query syntax than general-purpose S3
General-purpose S3 buckets cannot store Parquet files at all

On S3 Tables, AWS automatically runs compaction, snapshot management, and unreferenced-file cleanup; on general-purpose buckets, that maintenance is the user's own responsibility, typically via scheduled Glue jobs
questions.explain: The underlying format (Iceberg) is the same either way — the real difference is who performs the ongoing maintenance operations.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does Iceberg currently have the broader AWS footprint compared to Apache Hudi?
options: AWS has officially deprecated Hudi support
Iceberg is the only format that supports Parquet files
Hudi lacks native Redshift Spectrum support, while Iceberg has broader coverage across Athena, Glue, EMR, and S3 Tables itself
Hudi cannot be used with EMR at all
questions.explain: Hudi does have real AWS support (EMR, Glue 4.0+), but its coverage is narrower than Iceberg's — notably excluding native Redshift Spectrum support.
